name: Cadet Grey
lede: Cadet Grey is a soft, bluish grey, listed by one dictionary as a variant name for cadet blue.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines cadet blue as a bluish grey or strong blue, sometimes called cadet grey [3]. St Clair ties cadet blue to military uniforms, as a grey-greenish blue [4]. The record is thin, and no book we hold explains why cadets wore the color [3][4].

In the library the swatch is dated to 1912 in Maerz and Paul and sits in ISCC-NBS block 185, a family of dusty, greyish blues with many names [1]. It is close to [[grey]] and [[cadet-blue]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Cadet Grey appears in 1.94% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s at 1.6% of that century's paintings [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 46% of cases [2]. Its most devoted painter is Alfred Sisley, in 8 of 50 works here, 7.6 times the baseline [2].

origin.named_after: military cadet uniforms (cadet blue); the grey variant undocumented
